title: Carbonic Anhydrase Activity Assay
author: Jack C Koch
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.z8xf9xn
materials: Stock 50mM barbital buffer Mix 1 vial of barbital buffer (Sigma B5934-1VL) with 800 mL of deionized water. Once all powder is dissolved, add deionized water to 1L.

steps.title: Prepare Veronal Buffer A
steps.instruction: Mix 250 mL 50 mM barbital buffer with 250 mL deionized water and adjust the pH to 8.2 with 1 M HCl to obtain 25 mM Veronal Buffer (Buffer A).

steps.title: Prepare Extraction Buffer
steps.instruction: Mix 250 mL 50 mM barbital buffer with 250 mL deionized water, add 0.93 g EDTA and 1.23 g MgSO₄, stir until dissolved, then adjust pH to 8.2 with 1 M NaOH.

steps.title: Label Pipette Tips
steps.instruction: Take three new 1 mL pipette tips, label one “A” for Buffer A, one “E” for Extraction Buffer, and one “C” for CO₂‑saturated seawater; use a fresh set for each anemone native and denatured sample.

steps.title: Generate CO₂‑Saturated Water
steps.instruction: In a 500 mL flask containing 300 mL chilled DI water, bubble CO₂ through an air stone for 15 min, insert the rubber stopper, let equilibrate 15 min, then measure pH. Keep the flask on ice. If pH > 4.00, add 4–5 half‑dollar sized chunks of dry ice, loosely stopper, wait until dissolved, re‑measure, and repeat until pH < 4.00; finally tighten the stopper.

steps.title: Calibrate pH Probe
steps.instruction: Calibrate the pH probe daily according to the manufacturer’s specifications.

steps.title: Set Up Assay Vial
steps.instruction: Use a 6–12 mL sample vial (e.g., Thomas Scientific 60975L‑3, 224744, 224745, 60965D‑1, or 60965D‑3) equipped with a small stir bar; keep the vial on ice during measurements.

steps.title: Rinse Vial with Buffer A
steps.instruction: Rinse the vial with 1 mL Buffer A, discard the waste, and retain the stir bar.

steps.title: Add Buffer A to Vial
steps.instruction: Add 2 mL Buffer A to the vial using the “A” pipette tip.

steps.title: Prepare for pH Recording
steps.instruction: Place the vial on a stir plate, insert the pH probe (submerged, stir bar not contacting probe), and start the “read/log” function.

steps.title: Initiate CO₂ Reaction
steps.instruction: Quickly add 1 mL CO₂‑saturated seawater (using the “C” tip) to the vial, observe the pH decline, and continue recording for at least 120 s to ensure a rate of ~‑0.01 pH·s⁻¹.

steps.title: Clean Vial After Run
steps.instruction: Rinse the vial with DI water, discard the waste, and keep the stir bar.

steps.title: Save Data
steps.instruction: Transfer the recorded pH‑time data to a flash drive or computer log.

steps.title: Label Sample Tubes
steps.instruction: Label two 15 mL tubes (“Anemone ID native” and “Anemone ID denatured”) and two 1.5 mL tubes (“PROT Anemone ID” and “ALGAE Anemone ID”).

steps.title: Collect Anemone Tissue
steps.instruction: Remove 0.2 g–(½ to ⅛ of the animal) frozen tissue (minimum 0.2 g); cut a diagonal slice from the oral cavity to the edge, place it in the 1.5 mL “ALGAE” tube and freeze for later analysis; return the remaining tissue to the freezer.

steps.title: Homogenize Native Tissue
steps.instruction: Finely mince the remaining tissue, place it in a glass‑Teflon homogenizer with 3 mL Extraction Buffer, and grind on ice for 1–1.5 min until no visible chunks remain.

steps.title: Rinse Homogenizer
steps.instruction: Rinse the homogenizer with 4 mL Extraction Buffer, grind the rinse, and add it to the homogenate (total ≈ 7 mL).

steps.title: Centrifuge Homogenate
steps.instruction: Vortex briefly, then centrifuge at 4 °C, 4300 RCF for 10 min (balance tubes).

steps.title: Allocate Supernatant
steps.instruction: Transfer supernatant to the “native” 15 mL tube; add 3 mL of supernatant to the “denatured” tube; remove 200 µL–1 mL of supernatant and place it in the “PROT” tube, then freeze for protein assay.

steps.title: Prepare Boiling Water Bath
steps.instruction: Fill a 1000 mL beaker with ~900 mL DI water, place on a hot plate, and bring to a boil.

steps.title: Denature Sample
steps.instruction: Loosen caps of the denatured tubes slightly, suspend them in a floating holder above the boiling water so the homogenate is submerged, boil for 5 min, then remove and cool on ice for 5 min.

steps.title: Assay Native Sample – Replicate 1
steps.instruction: Rinse the assay vial with 1 mL Buffer A, add 1 mL Buffer A, vortex/pipette‑mix native homogenate, add 1 mL native homogenate, place on stir plate, insert probe, start read, add 1 mL CO₂‑saturated seawater, record for ≥120 s, then rinse with DI water.

steps.title: Assay Native Sample – Replicates 2‑3
steps.instruction: Repeat the native assay (steps in Replicate 1) two additional times with the same native sample to obtain three technical replicates.

steps.title: Assay Denatured Sample – Replicate 1
steps.instruction: Rinse the assay vial with 1 mL Buffer A, add 1 mL Buffer A, vortex/pipette‑mix denatured homogenate, add 1 mL denatured homogenate, place on stir plate, insert probe, start read, add 1 mL CO₂‑saturated seawater, record for ≥120 s, then rinse with DI water.

steps.title: Assay Denatured Sample – Replicates 2‑3
steps.instruction: Repeat the denatured assay (steps in Replicate 1) two additional times with the same denatured sample to obtain three technical replicates.

steps.title: Calculate CA Activity
steps.instruction: For each run, compute slope = (pH₂ − pH₁)/(time₂ − time₁); identify the most negative slope, average the three replicate slopes to obtain raw CA · s⁻¹, and convert to per minute (multiply by 60).

steps.title: Measure Protein Concentration
steps.instruction: Determine protein concentration of the “PROT” sample using a Bradford assay and express the result as mg mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Normalize CA Activity
steps.instruction: Divide the raw CA · minute⁻¹ by the protein concentration (mg mL⁻¹) to obtain ΔpH · minute⁻¹ · mg⁻¹ protein.
